claims.text: Machine-learning potentials trained on ab initio data can accurately predict fusion properties.
Machine-learning potentials trained on ab initio data can accurately predict high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The proposed machine-learning workflow has lower computational cost than explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed machine-learning workflow has lower computational cost than TOR-TILD.
Machine-learning potentials can be used to predict solid- and fluid-state free energies and associated thermodynamic properties.
The proposed method is applicable at high temperatures to multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The method can faithfully account for vibrational entropy and anharmonicity relevant to phase free energies.
The method can faithfully account for electron–vibration coupling relevant to phase free energies.
Machine-learning potentials can capture the complex interactions and correlations in the system.
Capturing these interactions and correlations enables accurate prediction of free energies and thermodynamic properties.
The proposed workflow will maintain accuracy comparable to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The proposed workflow will maintain accuracy comparable to TOR-TILD.
The stated composition boundary is elemental and binary systems.
The stated temperature boundary is above 1000 K.
Limited training data and bias in the machine-learning potentials may reduce reliability.

contradictions.description: The conditions identify multicomponent high-entropy systems as the target, whereas the boundary and initial-state fields restrict the stated domain to elemental and binary systems.
